chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.text:
You need to link your Google Ads account and your Merchant Center account before you can create Shopping campaigns. After you link the accounts, you'll be able to create a campaign that uses your product information. Product data in Merchant Center can also be used to power other add-ons, like promotions and custom reports.

By linking your Google Ads and Merchant Center accounts, you’ll be able to connect your Google Ads account to your Business Manager, which will automatically link to all other connected apps in the Business Manager account. This extends the capabilities of your Google Ads account, allowing you to promote your products and local stores.

Before you begin, ensure both your Google Ads and Merchant Center accounts don't have any account-level policy violations before linking.

Note: Linking to Business Manager can also be initiated in Google Ads by going to Tools , then Data manager, and selecting “Google Merchant Center”, under “Featured products”.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.text:
Note: To ensure the security of your Google Ads account, it's highly recommended to Turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google account. If 2-Step Verification is required, you’ll need to enable it or Disable the 2-Step Verification requirement in Google Ads before linking your account. Additionally, use a strong, unique password and regularly scan your computer for malware.

On this page

- Get started in Merchant Center

- Instructions for linking in Merchant Center

- Instructions for linking in Google Ads

- Manage links between accounts

- Data sharing

- Frequently asked questions

Note: In countries where the Comparison Shopping Services (CSS) program is available, you participate in Shopping ads through one or several CSSs of your choice. Some CSSs manage your product data and your campaigns on your behalf, while others provide tools allowing you to manage your setup yourself. Learn more About advertising with Comparison Shopping Services.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Get started in Merchant Center
chunks.text:
You can create a new Google Ads account or link to an existing one in Merchant Center. If you already have a Google Ads account associated with your Google Account, you can connect Merchant Center to that account right away.

When you link your Google Ads and Merchant Center accounts, your Google Ads account will automatically connect to Business Manager to connect all of the apps and services you use across Google. You can also choose to link only to your Merchant Center account.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Get started in Merchant Center > Option 1: Link to a Google Ads account you own in Merchant Center
chunks.text:
- Go to Access and services under "Settings" in the left navigation menu.

- Select Apps and services and then select Add service.

- Under "Select Google service", select Google Ads and select Next.

- In the pop-up window, select the Google Ads account you want to link.

- Select Next.

- Select Link to complete the link between your Google Ads account and Business Manager.

- If you only want to link your Google Ads account to your Merchant Center, select Link to Merchant Center only and then select Link.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Option 2: Create and link a new Google Ads account in Merchant Center
chunks.text:
- Go to Access and services under “Settings” in the left navigation menu.

- Select Apps and services and then select Add service.

- Select Google Ads and select Next.

- In the pop-up window, select New account. Modify any of the pre-populated details before proceeding and then select Next.

- Select Link to complete the link between your Google Ads account and Business Manager.

- If you only want to link your Google Ads account to your Merchant Center, select Link to Merchant Center only and then select Link.

Note: During the setup process, you’ll provide your time zone and currency. The options are pre-populated based on your location, but you can change the time zone and currency while you set up your account. After you create your account, you won’t be able to change these settings later.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Option 3: Link to a Google Ads account you don’t manage in Merchant Center
chunks.text: To link to a Google Ads account owned by other people (for example, agency partners), you’ll need the Google Ads customer ID (which is found at the top of any Google Ads page, near the account email address).

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Option 3: Link to a Google Ads account you don’t manage in Merchant Center > Step 1: Request link to Google Ads in Merchant Center
chunks.text:
- Go to Access and services under "Settings" in the left navigation menu.

- Select Apps and services and then select Add service.

- Select Google Ads and select Next.

- In the pop-up window, select the Account you don’t manage.

- Enter the Google Ads customer ID, then select Next.

- Select Send request to complete the link between your Google Ads account and Merchant Center.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Option 3: Link to a Google Ads account you don’t manage in Merchant Center > Step 2: Approve link request in Google Ads
chunks.text:
Link requests from Merchant Center need to be approved in the Google Ads account that you’re linking to. Someone with admin access to the Google Ads account should follow these steps to approve the link request:

- Go to Data manager within the "Tools" menu .

- Under “Connected products", find "Google Merchant Center”, then select Manage & link.

- Select the "Received" tab to view all the linking requests received.

- Find the account to link. The “Status” column will say “Needs your approval”.

- Select Review in the “Actions” column and review the request details.

- Select Approve.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Get started in Google Ads
chunks.text:
You can link to an existing Google Merchant Center account in Google Ads. If a Google Merchant Center account is already associated with your Google Account, you can immediately connect Google Ads to that account. If a Google Merchant Center account isn't directly associated with your Google Account, you can send a request to the Merchant Center account admin(s) for linking.

When you link your Google Ads and Merchant Center accounts, your Google Ads account will default to link to Business Manager to connect all of the apps and services you use across Google. You’ll also have the option to link only to your Merchant Center account.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Get started in Google Ads > Link to a Merchant Center account you own in Google Ads
chunks.text:
- Go to Data manager within the "Tools" menu .

- In the "Connected products" tab, find "Google Merchant Center" under "Featured products" section and select your preferred linking method.

- Select Next.

- Select Submit.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Get started in Google Ads > Link to a Merchant Center account you own in Google Ads > Approve link request in Google Merchant Center
chunks.text:
After you initiate a request to link your Merchant Center account from your Google Ads account, you’ll need to review and accept the link request within your Merchant Center account.

- In your Merchant Center account, select Settings in the left navigation menu.

- Select Access and services and go to the Apps and services tab.

- To approve a link request, select Accept in the “Action” column which is located in the “Third-party apps” tab.

Note:

- Make sure you have admin access in the Google Merchant Center account to accept the link request. Learn more about managing account links with partners.

- If you're an admin to both the Merchant Center and Ads account, the link is automatically approved.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Manage links between accounts
chunks.text:
After you've linked your Google Ads accounts, you can cancel the request, or unlink the accounts, or view the status of a link request in Merchant Center, Google Ads or Business Manager.

For a Google Ads account linked to Business Manager, super admins and Google Ads admins can unlink the accounts. To unlink a Google Ads account from Business Manager, follow these steps:

- In Business Manager, select the Apps and services section.

- Select the account you would like to remove.

- In the right side panel, select Remove access.

- When prompted, confirm that you’re unlinking the account.

Note: When you remove a Google Ads account from Business Manager, all of the apps in Business Manager will lose access to data from the Ads account.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Data sharing
chunks.text: When you connect your Google Ads Account to Merchant Center, some of your data is shared between them.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Data sharing > Data shared from Merchant Center
chunks.text:
- The name and ID of your Merchant Center account

- Product titles, descriptions, and images that show on Google Search and Maps

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Data sharing > Data shared from Ads
chunks.text:
- The name and account ID for your Google Ads account

- Clicks and conversions from your Campaigns, Ads, and Ad groups

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Who can initiate link requests to a Google Ads account?
chunks.text: Only someone with admin access in Merchant Center can initiate an account linking request. Ensure you're logged into the correct Merchant Center account with admin privileges. If you're using a manager account (MCC), verify that the MCC has ownership of the child accounts.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Who can approve link requests when I link to an existing Google Ads account?
chunks.text: Only someone with admin access to the account can approve the link request in Google Ads. If the correct user doesn't have admin access, an existing admin can grant it by going to "Tools & Settings," then "Setup," and "Access and Security" and assigning "Admin" level access.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Who can unlink a Google Ads account?
chunks.text:
For Google Ads accounts that are linked to Business Manager, a Google Ads account can only be unlinked by a super admin.

For Google Ads accounts that are linked to Merchant Center, the link can be removed at any time from Google Ads by anyone with admin access to the Google Ads account, or from Merchant Center by people with Merchant Center admin access. Other actions in the linked account may have additional access requirements (even if both accounts are linked). For example:

- People using Merchant Center can’t create or edit campaigns unless they have admin or standard access to the linked Google Ads account.

- A Google Ads account admin can’t edit or add products or create campaigns in Merchant Center unless they also have access to the linked Merchant Center account. (However, the Google Ads account admin can create campaigns from Google Ads.)

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > What happens when a Google Ads account is unlinked from Business Manager?
chunks.text: When you remove a Google Ads account from Business Manager, the Google Ads account will lose access to data from all of the apps connected in Business Manager. This means campaigns in Google Ads that rely on product information from the connected Merchant Center account and from connected Google Business Profiles will stop using your product information to serve ads. You also won’t be able to create new campaigns in Google Ads based on product information from these accounts. Google Ads will still continue to serve other campaign types, including Performance Max campaigns.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > What happens when a Google Ads account is unlinked from Merchant Center?
chunks.text: Campaigns in Google Ads that rely on product information from the Merchant Center account will stop using your product information to serve ads. You also won’t be able to create new campaigns in Google Ads based on product information from the unlinked Merchant Center account. Google Ads will still continue to serve other campaign types in the account.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Can I link a Google Ads manager account to Merchant Center?
chunks.text: No, you can’t link a Google Ads manager account to Merchant Center. A Google Ads manager account lets you view and manage multiple Google Ads accounts.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > How many Google Ads accounts can I link to a Merchant Center account or to my Business Manager?
chunks.text: A Merchant Center account can be linked to up to 500 Google Ads accounts. A Business Manager can have up to 20 Google Ads accounts linked to it.

chunks.title: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center
chunks.heading: Link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center > Can I link my campaign to multiple Merchant Center accounts?
chunks.text: No, you can only link a campaign to one Merchant Center account at a time. If you want to connect your campaign to a different Merchant Center account, you’ll need to create a new campaign.

chunks.title: Product and listing groups
chunks.heading: Product and listing groups
chunks.text:
Product groups are used in Shopping campaigns to organize your product inventory from Google Merchant Center. You create and manage product groups within your Google Ads Shopping campaign, using attributes derived from your product data. These groups allow you to set specific bids for different sets of products.

Learn how to Manage a Shopping campaign with product groups.

chunks.title: Product and listing groups
chunks.heading: Product and listing groups > Features of product group in Shopping campaigns
chunks.text:
Shopping campaigns use product groups to determine which items from your Merchant Center account appear on a search results page in a Shopping ad.

When you create a new Shopping campaign, a product group for "All products is created by default, using the default maximum cost-per-click bid (max. CPC) you set during ad group creation.

You can run your Shopping campaign using just the "All products product group, or subdivide it into as many product groups as you want by using product attributes like Google product category [google_product_category], product type [product_type], brand [brand], condition [condition], ID [id], and custom label 0-4 [custom label 0-4]. This allows you to target specific collections or exclude certain items. You can also remove product groups as needed. If you've recently added or updated custom labels in Merchant Center, allow 24-48 hours for them to be available for use in Google Ads product groups.

Each product can appear in only one biddable product group per ad group. You can also exclude a product from appearing in a product group entirely by using inventory filters or by setting its status to "Excluded within the listing group settings.

chunks.title: Product and listing groups
chunks.heading: Product and listing groups > Features of product group in Shopping campaigns
chunks.text:
If products are marked as "Excluded or "Not eligible and you want them to show, you'll need to change their status to 'Included'. Keep in mind that changes to product inclusion or eligibility can take 24-48 hours to sync between Merchant Center and Google Ads and reflect in your campaign.

Set and revise bids for each product group as often as you need, or exclude a product group from your campaign.

For Performance Max campaigns, reporting metrics can be different for the Product Groups tab when compared to the Campaign, Ad Group, or Ads tabs. This is because the Product Groups tab can only report on product level data.

- For example, when a Shopping ad shows many products in an individual ad slot, each product collects an impression. However, the campaign, ad group, and ad recognize that only a single ad was showing and will count it as one impression.

- Differences in impression counts between Performance Max item-level reports and campaign-level reports are expected. This is because item-level reporting focuses specifically on Shopping inventory and doesn't represent all the channels where a Performance Max campaign can serve.

chunks.title: Negative keyword: Definition
chunks.heading: Negative keyword: Definition
chunks.text:
A type of keyword that prevents your ad from being triggered by a certain word or phrase. Your ads aren’t shown to anyone who is searching for that phrase. This is also known as a negative match.

For example, when you add "free" as a negative keyword to your campaign or ad group, you tell Google Ads not to show your ad for any search containing the term "free." On the Display Network, your ad is less likely to appear on a site when your negative keywords match the site's content.

chunks.title: Use Keyword Planner
chunks.heading: Use Keyword Planner
chunks.text:
Google Keyword Planner helps you research keywords for your Search campaigns.

You can use the Google Keyword Planner tool to discover new keywords related to your business and view estimates of the searches they receive and the cost to target them.

Keyword Planner also provides another way to create Search campaigns that’s centered around in-depth Google keyword research.

This article shows you how to use Keyword Planner to lay the groundwork for a successful campaign.

How to use Google Keyword Planner: Find the Best Keywords for Your Business

On this page

- Benefits of Keyword Planner

- How to use Keyword Planner

- Create a keyword plan

- Understand your keyword forecast

- Organize keywords into ad groups (English only)

chunks.title: Use Keyword Planner
chunks.heading: Use Keyword Planner > Benefits of Keyword Planner
chunks.text:
- Discover new keywords: Get suggestions for keywords related to your products, services, or website.

- View monthly searches: View estimates on the number of searches a keyword gets each month with a comprehensive Google keyword research tool.

- Determine cost: View the average cost for your ad to show on searches for a keyword.

- Organize keywords: View how your keywords fit into different categories related to your brand.

- Create new campaigns: Use your keyword plan to create new campaigns centered on in-depth keyword research.

Google Keyword Planner can provide insights into keyword targeting, and offer traffic estimates of keyword campaigns. However, campaign performance depends on a variety of factors. For example, your bid, budget, ad quality, location targeting, product, abuse trends, and customer behavior in your industry can all influence the success of your campaigns and monetization of keywords.

chunks.title: Use Keyword Planner

Discover new keywords

chunks.title: Use Keyword Planner
chunks.heading: Use Keyword Planner > How to use Keyword Planner > 1. Create a keyword plan > A. Get ideas for new keywords

- There are 2 ways to discover new keyword ideas:

- Start with keywords: Enter words related to your products or services. You can separate multiple phrases with a comma and space.

- Start with a website: Enter any website and Google will look for keywords related to the content on that site. Note: the contents of hyperlinks aren’t used to generate keyword ideas.

- Select Get results.

Tip: Specifying a keyword and a URL can result in a larger volume of keyword ideas, as compared to just URL.

After selecting “Get results”, you’ll find a list of keywords related to what you entered. You can then add these keywords to your plan. You can now edit your list with filters and categories to help you find those that make sense for your plan.

chunks.title: Use Keyword Planner

chunks.title: Use Keyword Planner
chunks.heading: Use Keyword Planner > How to use Keyword Planner > 2. Understand your keyword forecast
chunks.text:
Your plan forecast shows you how many conversions, clicks, or impressions you’re likely to get for your keywords based on your spend. Learn more About Keyword Planner forecasts

Tip: If market changes affect you, we recommend planning weekly rather than monthly or quarterly until markets stabilize.

Keyword Planner’s forecasts are refreshed daily and based on the last 7–10 days, adjusted for seasonality. Your forecasts will take into account any impact of market changes during this time frame. We’ve updated our seasonal model to account for current market conditions.

chunks.title: Use Keyword Planner

chunks.text:
Your forecast is available on the “Forecasts” page of your plan. It includes keywords that you uploaded through “Get search volumes and forecasts” or those you added from the “Keyword ideas” page.

What’s included in your forecast

- Change the metric you’re forecasting by selecting “Conversions” or “Clicks”. This is available to you when you enable conversion tracking in your account. Otherwise, select "Add conversion metrics" to review the options.

Additional options

chunks.title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns
chunks.heading: About Quality Score for Search campaigns
chunks.text:
Quality Score is a diagnostic tool meant to give you a sense of how well your ad quality compares to other advertisers.

This score is measured on a scale from 1-10 and available at the keyword level. A higher Quality Score means that your ad and landing page are more relevant and useful to someone searching for your keyword, compared to other advertisers.

You can use the Quality Score diagnostic tool to identify where it might be beneficial to improve your ads, landing pages, or keyword selection.

On this page

- Calculate Quality Score

- Check Quality Score

Good to know about Quality Score

- Quality Score is not a key performance indicator and should not be optimized or aggregated with the rest of your data.

- Quality Score is not an input in the ad auction. It’s a diagnostic tool to identify how ads that show for certain keywords affect the user experience.

chunks.title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns
chunks.heading: About Quality Score for Search campaigns > How it’s calculated
chunks.text:
Quality Score is calculated based on the combined performance of 3 components:

- Expected clickthrough rate (CTR): The likelihood that your ad will be clicked when shown.

- Ad relevance: How closely your ad matches the intent behind a user's search.

- Landing page experience: How relevant and useful your landing page is to people who click your ad.

Each component is evaluated with a status of “Above average,” “Average,” or “Below average.” This evaluation is based on a comparison with other advertisers whose ads showed for the exact same search over the last 90 days.

A broad match keyword may have a Quality Score even though it has no impressions as long as there is a corresponding exact match keyword with impressions in the last 90 days. If there are impressions for searches that exactly match a broad match keyword through an exact match keyword in the same ad group, this will report the same Quality Score for both of the keywords.

If one of these components has a status of “Average” or “Below average”, this may indicate an opportunity to make improvements. Learn more about 5 ways to use Quality Score to improve your performance.

chunks.title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns
chunks.heading: About Quality Score for Search campaigns > How it’s calculated > Keep in mind
chunks.text:
- Quality Score is based on historical impressions for exact searches of your keyword, therefore changing keyword match types will not impact Quality Score.

- If you notice a “—” in the Quality Score column, it means there aren't enough searches that exactly match your keywords to determine a keyword’s Quality Score. To help gather traffic data and resolve this status:

- Use Keyword Planner to discover higher-volume keywords: Identify relevant search terms with sufficient search volume.

- Broaden match types: While match types don't change how your Quality Score is calculated, broadening them helps your keyword participate in more auctions, increasing the chances of gathering enough exact-match search data to generate a score.

- There are factors related to your ad quality that might not be captured by Quality Score. These factors include, but are not limited to:

- Devices used in search

- Location of user

- Time of day

- Assets

- Information obtained from any of Google's various crawlersmay be used to assess ad quality, which can be reflected through Quality Score.

chunks.title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns
chunks.heading: About Quality Score for Search campaigns > How to check your Quality Score
chunks.text:
- Go to Keywords within the Campaigns menu .

- In the upper right corner of the table, select the columns icon .

- Under “Modify columns for keywords”, select the drop-down arrow beside “All columns” and open the Quality score section.

- To add the current Quality Score and its component statuses as new columns in the keyword reporting table, select any of the following:

- Quality Score

- Landing Page Exp.

- Exp. CTR

- Ad Relevance

- To view past Quality Score stats for the reporting period you’re looking at, choose any of the following metrics. To add past Quality Score data and its component statuses as new columns in the keyword reporting table, select the following:

- Quality Score (hist.)

- Landing Page Exper. (hist.)

- Ad Relevance (hist.)

- Exp. CTR. (hist.)

You can view the change in daily scores by segmenting your table by day.

- Select Apply.

chunks.title: Auction
chunks.heading: Auction
chunks.text:
The process that happens with each Google search to decide which ads will appear for that specific search and in which order those ads will show on the page (or whether or not any ads will show at all).

- Each time an ad is eligible to appear for a search, it goes through the ad auction. The auction determines whether or not the ad actually shows and in which ad position it will show on the page.

- Here's how the auction works:

- When someone searches, the Google Ads system finds all ads whose keywords match that search.

- From those ads, the system ignores any that aren't eligible, like ads that target a different country or are disapproved based on a policy violation.

- Of the remaining ads, only those with a sufficiently high Ad Rank may show. Ad Rank is a combination of your bid, ad quality, the Ad Rank thresholds, the context of the person's search, and the expected impact of extensions and other ad formats.

- The most important thing to remember is that even if your competition bids higher than you, you can still win a higher position -- at a lower price -- with highly relevant keywords and ads.

chunks.title: Auction
chunks.heading: Auction
chunks.text:
- Since the auction process is repeated for every search on Google, each auction can have potentially different results depending on the competition at that moment. Therefore it's normal for you to see some fluctuation in your ad's position on the page and in whether or not your ad shows at all.

About ad position

chunks.title: Different ways to track conversions
chunks.heading: Different ways to track conversions
chunks.text:
When you run ads with Google Ads, you may want to know whether clicks on your ad led customers to take certain actions such as making a purchase on your website, calling your business, or downloading your app.

The first step in measuring conversions is choosing what you want to track. Learn more about setting up your conversions.

You can also set up multiple conversion actions for each conversion source. For example, if you want to track both purchases and newsletter sign-ups on your website, create one conversion action for purchases and another for sign-ups.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.text:
After you’ve set up conversion tracking, you can gain more insights by adding reporting columns to discover how your ads lead to valuable customer actions.

Columns in your conversion summary provide a variety of information about your account. You can customize your view by adding specific columns. Choose which columns to display, then rearrange and save them in your preferred order.

Below, you'll find what these metrics mean and how to add them to your reports.

On this page

- "Conversions" and related columns

- Track "All conversions" and "Cross-device conversions"

- Time of conversion

- About view-through conversions

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > "Conversions" and related columns
chunks.text:
- Go to Summary within the Goals menu .

- Hover over the title at the top of each column for a definition of the conversion action.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > "Conversions" and related columns > “Conversions” column
chunks.text:
The "Conversions" column shows the number of conversions that you've received across your primary conversion actions. Conversions are measured with conversion tracking and may include modeled conversions in cases where you aren’t able to observe all conversions. Use this column to view how often your ads lead customers to actions that you’ve defined as valuable for your business. This column is generally used for bidding optimization. If you're looking for data that includes secondary conversion actions or view-through conversions, refer to the "All conversions" column.

You can customize how the data in your "Conversions" column is tracked:

- "Account-default conversion goals" setting: If you’re tracking a conversion action but don’t want to include its data in the column, you can uncheck this setting. By default, most conversion actions are included, so in most cases, all of your conversion actions are included in your "Conversions" column unless you've unchecked the setting. Learn more About account-default conversion goals.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > "Conversions" and related columns > “Conversions” column
chunks.text:
- Campaign-level conversion setting: You can specify conversion actions for a particular campaign or a group of campaigns using the campaign conversion setting. Learn more About account-default conversion goals.

- "Attribution model" setting: For website and Google Analytics conversion actions, you can choose how much credit each of a customer's clicks gets for each conversion. Learn more About attribution models.

- Conversion counting setting: You can choose to count every conversion after an interaction, or only one conversion after an interaction. Select "Every" for sales to track each purchase and "One" for leads to prevent duplicate counts from page refreshes. Use "Transaction IDs" to deduplicate sales and ensure only bottom-of-funnel actions are set as "Primary" to avoid inflating counts. Learn more About conversion counting settings.

Tip: "Conversions" and bidding

If you're optimizing your bids for conversions through automated or manual bid strategies, the data in the "Conversions" column is used for your bidding strategies.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > "Conversions" and related columns > “Conversions” column
chunks.text: Important: Frequent manual adjustments to budgets, targets (CPA or ROAS), or conversion goals will reset the standard 7-14 day learning period and delay campaign optimization. To prevent ad serving delays and allow the system to stabilize, it is recommended to avoid making further changes during this optimization window.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > "Conversions" and related columns > Explore related columns
chunks.text:
Understanding the distinction between these reporting columns allows you to use the "Conversions" column as a focused signal for Smart Bidding optimization, while utilizing "All conversions" for a comprehensive view of your business performance. This separation ensures your bidding strategies focus on your primary goals without losing visibility into secondary actions.

Besides the main “Conversions” column, there are several related columns that use your “Conversions” data to provide more information:

- Cost per conversion (“Cost / conv.”) tells you how much, on average, each of your conversions cost. It’s calculated by dividing your total cost by the number in your “Conversions” column. This calculation only applies to eligible interactions, like ad clicks or video ad views, so any clicks that can’t be tracked for conversions are removed from the calculation.

- Conversion rate (“Conv. rate”) tells you how often, on average, an ad click or other ad interaction leads to a conversion. It’s calculated by dividing “Conversions” by the total eligible interactions, for example, ad clicks or video ad views.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > "Conversions" and related columns > Explore related columns
chunks.text:
- Total conversion value (“Total conv. value”) is the sum of conversion values for your “Conversions.” You have to enter a value for your conversion actions to make this metric useful.

- Troubleshooting incorrect values: If values are missing or defaulting to $1.00, ensure "Use different values for each conversion" is selected in settings. For dynamic values (for example, Shopify or WooCommerce), verify that variables are correctly mapped in your Google Tag Manager data layer or event snippet. For offline conversions, ensure your upload template includes the "Conversion Value" column.

- Keep in mind: In the new Google Ads experience, this column is called "Conv. value". Determine which Google Ads experience you're using.

- Conversion value per cost (“Conv. value / cost”) estimates your return on investment. It’s calculated by dividing your total conversion value by the total cost of all ad interactions.

- Conversion value per click (“Conv. value / click”) is your total conversion value divided by the number of eligible clicks.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > "Conversions" and related columns > Explore related columns
chunks.text:
- Conversion value per click (“Conv. value / click”) is your total conversion value divided by the number of eligible clicks.

- Value per conversion (“Value / conv.”) tells you approximately how much, on average, each of your conversions is worth. It’s calculated by dividing your total conversion value by the number in your “Conversions” column. This metric is useful if each of your conversions has a different value.

- Conversion value rules (“All conv. value”) shows the combined value for each conversion action. For example: Say you've set the value of a newsletter signup as $3, and you've gotten 10 signups. Your “All conv. value” will be $30. If you’d like to review specific conversion value rules reporting, you can segment your reports.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > Track "All conversions" and "Cross-device conversions"
chunks.text:
"All conversions" ("All conv.") shows comprehensive data for all primary and secondary conversion actions, and includes other special conversion sources, such as view-through conversions. This column provides a comprehensive view of all actions tracked, regardless of whether they're used directly for bidding. If you're comparing Google Ads data with third-party platforms, or your own systems, using "All conv. (by conv. time)" may give you a better comparison. This is because it reports conversions by the time they occurred, rather than the time of the ad click.

“All conversions” has the same set of related columns as “Conversions,” but with metrics calculated based on your “All conversions” column instead of “Conversions.” These columns include:

- Cost per all conversions (“Cost / all conv.”)

- All conversion rate (“All conv. rate”)

- All conversion value (“All conv. value”)

- All conversion value per cost (“All conv. value / cost”)

- All conversion value per click (“All conv. value / click”)

- Value per all conversions (“Value / all conv.”)

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > Track "All conversions" and "Cross-device conversions"
chunks.text:
- All conversion value per click (“All conv. value / click”)

- Value per all conversions (“Value / all conv.”)

The "Cross-device conversions" ("Cross-device conv.") column shows the total number of cross-device conversions across all of your conversion actions. Cross-device conversions start with a click on an ad from one device and end with a conversion on another device or in a different web browser on the same device.

To give you a more complete report of cross-device conversions, Google uses models based on privacy-safe data from users who've previously signed into Google services. These models predict cross-device conversions that can’t be directly observed. This allows us to provide reporting on cross-device behavior that combines observed and modeled conversions, without compromising user privacy.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > Track "All conversions" and "Cross-device conversions" > Decimals in conversion data
chunks.text:
You may notice that the numbers in your "Conversions," "All conversions," and "Cross-device conversions" columns have 2 decimal places. This is because data-driven attribution (DDA) and other attribution models attribute fractional credit for each conversion across multiple clicks. These fractions are represented as decimals like 0.33 or 0.50. Even without using an attribution model that reports fractional conversions, your conversion data would still show 2 decimals like .00 for accuracy.

Decimals or "fractional credits" often appear when using attribution models like data-driven attribution. This reflects the reality of multi-touch customer journeys, where credit for a single conversion is distributed across multiple ad interactions that contributed to the final action. Learn more About attribution models.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > Track "All conversions" and "Cross-device conversions" > Dashes in conversion data
chunks.text: You may notice a dash (“-”) instead of a numeric value for conversion totals or daily values in account-level charts and campaign summaries. This occurs when specific campaign types that use unique conversion measurement methods are included in an aggregated view. Because these conversion types can’t be combined in a normal sum, a dash is displayed to maintain data accuracy and avoid incorrect aggregation across different campaign types.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > Time of conversion
chunks.text:
The primary conversion columns mentioned above are calculated based on the time of the click, not the time of the conversion. For example, if your ad was clicked on last week and that traffic converted this week, both the click and the conversion are reported back to last week in the primary conversions columns. This allows you to accurately measure metrics like cost per conversion or return on ad spend, because ad spend is also calculated based on the time of the click.

You can also report on conversions based on the time the conversion occurred. This is helpful when comparing your Google Ads data with third-party analytics like Google Analytics or Shopify. Discrepancies, often up to 20%, are expected due to different attribution models (for example, Google Analytics often uses last-click vs. Google Ads click-date attribution). When comparing with Google Analytics, ensure reports are set to "Event-scoped" and verify GCLID persistence. Using "All conv. (by conv. time)" helps reconcile differences between click-date and conversion-date reporting. Note that reporting lags can take up to 24-48 hours. Time of conversion columns include:

- “Conversions (by conv. time)”

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > Time of conversion
chunks.text:
- “Conversions (by conv. time)”

- “Conv. value (by conv. time)”

- “Value / Conv. (by conv. time)”

- “All conv. (by conv. time)”

- “All conv. value (by conv. time)”

- “Value / all conv. (by conv. time)”

Note: Data for these columns is available from March 2019. Store visit conversions and store sales conversions aren't included in the “by conv. time” column data. Even when using these columns, differences may still exist due to varying attribution models, lookback windows, and how each platform processes data. To compare data fairly between Google Analytics and Google Ads, navigate to the Google Analytics Advertising section or filter reports for “Session source / medium” set to google / cpc. Keep in mind that Google Analytics defaults to data-driven attribution, while Google Ads uses ad-centric models. Additionally, always account for the 24–48 hour processing delay before comparing final results.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > About view-through conversions
chunks.text:
Your “View-through conversions” column tells you when customers view, but don’t interact with your ad, and later complete a conversion on your site. This is different from the data in your other conversion columns, which record when customers interact with an ad and then complete a conversion on your site.

View-through conversions are a helpful way to track the value of your display or video ad campaigns. For display campaigns, for example, they measure the conversions where a customer views an ad but doesn't click it before completing a conversion. View-through conversions take into account the settings of your conversion actions, such as how conversions are counted.

For Display Network ads, the last viewable impression gets credit for the view-through conversion. With Google's Active View technology, an impression of a display ad is considered viewable when at least 50% of the ad is onscreen for at least 1 second.

View-through conversions automatically exclude conversions from people who have also interacted with any of your other ads. View-through conversions are not included in the “Conversions” column, only in the “View-through conversions” and "All conversions" columns.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > About view-through conversions
chunks.text: View-through conversions from browsers that don’t allow cross-site cookies can't be reported.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > About view-through conversions > View-through conversions for video ads
chunks.text:
For video campaigns, view-through conversions tell you when an impression of your video ad leads to a conversion on your site. The last impression of a video ad gets credit for the view-through conversion.

Keep in mind: An impression is different from a “view” of a video ad. A “view” is counted when someone watches 30 seconds or the full ad if it’s shorter than 30 seconds, or clicks on a part of the ad. A “view” that leads to a conversion is counted in the “Conversions” column.

chunks.title: Understand your conversion tracking data
chunks.heading: Understand your conversion tracking data > About view-through conversions > View-through conversions for App Connect
chunks.text:
For web campaigns using App Connect, you can track VTC for in-app conversions following an ad view, even if the user didn’t directly click or engage with the ad. This capability is focused on "Active Views" across YouTube, Display, and Gmail. On the Google Display Network, for instance, an Active View is counted only when at least 50% of the ad is displayed for at least one continuous second.

By default, VTC for App Connect utilizes a 24-hour lookback window. While these conversions are strictly for reporting and remain non-biddable on Display channels, the system is designed to prioritize app campaigns and Google TV Masthead campaigns over web campaigns. This ensures accurate attribution and prevents duplicate conversion counting across your campaigns.

chunks.title: Conversion action: Definition
chunks.heading: Conversion action: Definition
chunks.text:
Conversion action: A specific customer action that you've defined as valuable to your business, such as an online purchase or phone call. Tracking conversion actions lets you see how your ads lead to those valuable actions.

- Conversion actions are available for several conversion sources, including website actions, calls, app downloads, and in-app actions (such as in-app purchases).

- If you want to track more than one of the same kind of conversion action, such as a newsletter signup and a lead form submission on your website, you can create multiple conversion actions.

- Occurrences of conversion actions are reported as conversions.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions
chunks.text:
Enhanced conversions is a feature that can improve the accuracy of your conversion measurement and unlock more powerful bidding. It supplements your existing conversion by sending hashed first party conversion data (from your website tags or your imported offline events) to Google in a privacy safe way. The feature uses a secure one-way hashing algorithm called SHA256 on your first party customer data, such as email addresses, before sending to Google. You can learn more about Google’s conversion modeling solutions.

Note: Google is committed to protecting the confidentiality and security of your data. We'll keep your data confidential and secure using the same industry-leading standards we use to protect our own users’ data. We only report privacy-safe conversions. You can read more about enhanced conversions customer data policies and how we use your data.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions > How it works
chunks.text:
When a customer converts on your website, you may receive first-party customer data such as an email address, name, home address, and/or phone number. This data can be captured in your conversion tracking tags, hashed, sent to Google in its hashed form, and then used to enhance your conversion measurement.

If you decide to normalize and hash the data, follow the below instructions.

For normalization:

- Remove leading and trailing whitespaces.

- Convert the text to lowercase.

- Format phone numbers according to the E.164 standard.

- Remove all periods (.) that precede the domain name in gmail.com and googlemail.com email addresses.

For hash:

- Use hex SHA256.

Depending on which type of enhanced conversions you use, the hashed data will be used in different ways to improve your measurement:

Enhanced conversions for web
 Enhanced conversions for leads

Relevant for advertisers who want to track sales and events that happen on a website.

Relevant for advertisers who want to track sales that happen off a website (for example an online inquiry for an apartment) from website leads.

Improves measurement of online conversions.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions > How it works
chunks.text:
Improves measurement of online conversions.

Improves measurement of offline transactions that came from a website lead or visitor.

Allows you to send hashed first-party, user-provided data from your website when a user converts. The data is then used to match your customers to Google accounts, which were signed-in to when they engaged with one of your ads.

Allows you to use hashed, first-party user-provided data from your website (e.g., lead forms) together with imported offline lead conversions. When you import your leads, the provided hashed information is used to attribute back to the Google Ad campaign by matching to the data collected on your website and to signed-in Google accounts that engaged with your ads.

Configure enhanced conversions for web
 Configure enhanced conversions for leads

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.text:
Important: Enhanced conversions for web and leads are now combined into a single on/off setting. Starting from April 2026, Google Ads accepts user-provided data from website tags, Data Manager, and API connections, and you will no longer need to choose between different implementation methods. Existing users will be automatically migrated to the new unified setting. Learn more about the Updates to your enhanced conversions settings.

Enhanced conversions is a feature that can improve the accuracy of your conversion measurement and unlock more powerful bidding. Learn more About enhanced conversions.

You can set up enhanced conversions at the account level in your Google Ads account. This means that you’ll be able to turn on enhanced conversions for your entire account and reduce the number of steps it takes to set up enhanced conversions.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > On this page
chunks.text:
- Before you begin

- How this change impacts your conversion actions

- How this change impacts your Google tag settings

- Select your implementation method at the account level

- Opt in or out of enhance conversions at the account level

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > Before you begin
chunks.text:
Enhanced conversions is available as an account level setting. You’ll have enhanced conversions enabled in your account if:

- You had already set up enhanced conversions at the conversion action level previously.

- You only have one implementation method (across your existing conversion actions) that has enhanced conversions enabled. For example, if you only use the Google tag or the Google Ads API as the implementation method.

- You have both tag implementation methods (across your existing conversion actions) that have enhanced conversions enabled. Specifically, if you use the Google tag and Google Tag Manager implementation methods.

If you haven’t set up enhanced conversions, review About enhanced conversions to learn more about how to set up enhanced conversions for web or for leads.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > How this change impacts your conversion actions
chunks.text: With account-level enhanced conversions, your conversion actions may exhibit different behaviors based on the way they have been set up in Google Ads. Review the details below to learn more about how enhanced conversions at the account level will impact you.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > How this change impacts your conversion actions > Existing conversion actions
chunks.text:
Existing conversion actions that already had enhanced conversions turned on will continue to benefit from enhanced conversions at the account-level.

Existing conversion actions that didn’t have enhanced conversions turned on will get it enabled with account-level enhanced conversions, unless the conversion action was previously explicitly opted out of enhanced conversions.

Note that you can also take additional steps to ensure enhanced conversions data is being provided appropriately through tag setup or the API setup. Depending on the implementation, you can review these instructions for Google tag, Google Tag Manager or Google Ads API.

Important: If you're migrating from action-level to account-level enhanced conversions, ensure that your action-level configurations are removed. Google Ads prioritizes action-level settings. Therefore, residual configurations can conflict with your new account-level setup. This conflict may result in dropped enhanced conversion pings.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > How this change impacts your conversion actions > New conversion actions
chunks.text: New conversion actions inherit the account-level settings for enhanced conversions. For example, if enhanced conversions is turned on at the account-level and automatic collection is being used, new conversion actions also have enhanced conversions turned on with automatic collection by default.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > How this change impacts your Google tag settings
chunks.text: With enhanced conversions at the account level, Google tag settings for enhanced conversions are available globally across all conversion actions, rather than individually for each conversion action. This means that enhanced conversions share the same tag-wide settings as all other Google Ads features and tag destinations, such as enhanced conversions for leads and Google Analytics.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > How this change impacts your Google tag settings > New Google tag settings
chunks.text: If you haven’t yet configured any Google tag settings for products or features outside of enhanced conversions, new global settings will automatically be created for your tag by combining your existing conversion action level enhanced conversion tag settings. These Google tag settings will be applied to all conversion actions using enhanced conversions, and will also be shared across any Google products or features that use your tag in the future.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > How this change impacts your Google tag settings > Existing Google tag settings
chunks.text:
If you’ve already configured Google tag settings for other products or features, such as enhanced conversions for leads or Google Analytics, your Google tag settings from enhanced conversions at the conversion action level will automatically be combined and merged into your existing tag-level settings:

- Allow user-provided data capabilities: The existing tag-level setting will be respected. It's recommended to keep these settings enabled for Google Ads to receive data from enhanced conversions. Review these instructions to ensure enhanced conversions data is being provided appropriately through your tag setup.

- Automatically detect user-provided data: The existing tag-level setting will be respected.

- Exclusion CSS selectors for automatic collection: All CSS selectors will be combined into one list.

- Specify CSS selectors and JavaScript variables: All CSS Selectors and JavaScript variables for “Email”, “Phone number”, and “Name and address” will be combined into one list.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > How this change impacts your Google tag settings > Manage your Google tag settings
chunks.text: You can manage all of your Google tag settings and destinations at any time from the Google Ads Data Manager. You can also access your Google tag settings from the enhanced conversions account level settings.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > Select your implementation method at the account level
chunks.text:
Some existing enhanced conversions customers need to select a method for collecting user-provided data in order to upgrade their account to enhanced conversions at the account-level. The method you select for account-level enhanced conversions will be applied to all new and existing conversion actions. As a result, all other methods will no longer collect user-provided data for enhanced conversions, so we recommend choosing the method you are using the most today for enhanced conversions to avoid any changes in your enhanced conversions performance.

There are 3 available methods to choose from: Google tag, Google Tag Manager, or Google Ads API. If your account currently uses both Google tag and Google Tag Manager for enhanced conversions across your conversion actions, try following these instructions to set up your Google tag in Google Tag Manager. Then, you can use Google Tag Manager to collect user-provided data for all of your conversion actions.

Follow the steps below to upgrade your account to account-level enhanced conversions in Google Ads:

- Go to Settings within the Goals menu .

- Expand the “Enhanced conversions” section.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > Select your implementation method at the account level
chunks.text:
- Go to Settings within the Goals menu .

- Expand the “Enhanced conversions” section.

- Choose a method for setting up and managing user-provided data.

If no action is taken by October 2025, Google will automatically select a method based on your current enhanced conversions setup and upgrade your account to use enhanced conversions at the account level.

chunks.title: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads
chunks.heading: About enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads > Opt in or out of enhanced conversions at the account level
chunks.text:
If you have conversion actions that aren’t switched to account-level enhanced conversions, you can opt them in from your Google Ads account. Learn more about how to Opt into enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads.

If you decide that enhanced conversions at the account-level doesn’t work for you, you can opt out of specific conversion actions. Learn more about how to Opt out of enhanced conversions at the account level in Google Ads.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models
chunks.text:
Note: The first click, linear, time decay, and position-based attribution models are no longer supported by Google. Conversion actions that used the deprecated attribution models have been upgraded to use data-driven attribution. You can also switch to the last click model, which is still supported.

On the path to conversion, customers may interact with multiple ads from the same advertiser. Attribution models let you choose how much credit each ad interaction gets for your conversions.

Attribution models can give you a better understanding of how your ads perform and can help you optimize across conversion journeys.

This article describes the various attribution models and how to use them in Google Ads. You'll learn how to set an attribution model for conversion tracking and bidding, and how to compare models with the "Model comparison" attribution report.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > Benefits
chunks.text:
Most advertisers are used to measuring the success of their online advertising on a "last click" basis. This means they give all the credit for a conversion to the last-clicked ad and corresponding keyword. However, this ignores the other ad interactions customers may have had along the way.

Attribution models give you more control over how much credit each ad interaction gets for your conversions. This allows you to:

- Reach customers earlier in the purchase cycle: Find opportunities to influence customers earlier on their path to conversion.

- Match your business: Use a model that works best for how people search for what you offer.

- Improve your bidding: Optimize your bids based on a better understanding of how your ads perform.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > About the different attribution models
chunks.text:
Google Ads currently offers several attribution models:

Last click: Gives all credit for the conversion to the last-clicked ad and corresponding keyword.

Data-driven: Distributes credit for the conversion based on your past data for this conversion action. It's different from the other models, in that it uses your account's data to calculate the actual contribution of each interaction across the conversion path. The "Data-driven" model is the default attribution model for most conversion actions. Learn more about data-driven attribution.

Note: When you convert in-app, we may attribute it to App campaigns for reporting purposes.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > About the different attribution models > Example
chunks.text:
You own a restaurant called Ristorante Abigaille in Florence, Italy. A customer finds your site by clicking on your ads after performing each of these searches: "restaurant tuscany," "restaurant florence," "3 star restaurant florence," and then "3 star restaurant abigaille florence." She makes a reservation after clicking on your ad that appeared with "3 star restaurant abigaille florence."

- In the "Last click" attribution model, the last keyword, "3 star restaurant abigaille florence," would receive 100% of the credit for the conversion.

- In the "Data-driven" attribution model, each keyword would receive part of the credit, depending on how much it contributed to driving the conversion.

To learn how to compare these attribution models and view how they'd affect your data, check the section on the "Model comparison" report below.

Your account can contain conversions with the following creditable channels:

- Google paid channels: Google Ads channels can receive credit for a conversion.

- Paid channels: Paid media channels can receive credit for a conversion.

- Paid and organic channels: Both paid and organic channels can receive credit for a conversion.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > About the different attribution models > Example
chunks.text:
- Paid and organic channels: Both paid and organic channels can receive credit for a conversion.

- [Publisher] channels: Only [publisher] channels can receive credit for a conversion.

- Unknown channels: These conversions are assigned credit by their data source.

Creditable channels are those that are eligible to receive credit for a conversion. If you set up conversions in multiple Google products, your creditable channels for those conversions may differ depending on the other activity measured in that account. You can find the creditable channels for your conversions alongside the "Attribution Model" setting in Google Ads, Google Analytics, Search Ads 360, Display & Video 360, and Campaign Manager.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > About attribution models for conversions and bidding
chunks.text:
The "Attribution model" setting in conversion tracking lets you decide how to attribute conversions for each conversion action. You can use this setting for website and Google Analytics conversion actions. Learn How to find and set an attribution model for your conversions.

This setting affects how conversions are counted in your "Conversions" and "All conversions" columns. (Keep in mind that the "Conversions" column only includes those conversion actions you've marked as primary conversions.)

The attribution model you choose only affects the conversion action to which it's applied. The setting also affects any bid strategies that use the data in the "Conversions" column. This means that if you use an automated bid strategy that optimizes for conversions, such as Target cost per action (Target CPA), Enhanced cost-per-click (ECPC), or Target return on ad spend (Target ROAS), the attribution model you select will affect how your bids are optimized.

If you use manual bidding strategies, you can change your attribution model to help you set your bids.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > About attribution models for conversions and bidding
chunks.text:
If you use manual bidding strategies, you can change your attribution model to help you set your bids.

If you're not sure what model to choose, check the section below on the "Model comparison" report, which lets you compare different attribution models. When you're trying a new non-last click attribution model, we recommend that you test the model first and assess how it affects your return on investment.

If you experience issues like conversions not being recorded, or an “Inactive” status for your conversion actions after changing models or during setup, verify that your Google tags are correctly implemented on all relevant pages, especially thank you/confirmation pages. Use Google Tag Assistant to diagnose tag issues and ensure the Conversion Linker tag is active if you're using Google Tag Manager. Performing test conversions can also help identify problems.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > About attribution models for conversions and bidding
chunks.text: Note: Changing your attribution model from "Last click" to "Data-driven" helps determine which of your ad interactions are most impactful. Data-driven attribution assigns a value to each ad interaction that has contributed to the conversion process and helps drive additional conversions at the same CPA. Learn How to change bids and targets after switching models from "Last click" to "Data-driven".

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > About the "Model comparison" report
chunks.text:
Note: In the "Model comparison report," you might notice a message about historical data being only partially available for your selected date range. This could be because your account has only recently become eligible for cross-network attribution. To provide accurate performance metrics, the report filters out any network or campaign without enough data. Select a more recent date range to get complete data.

The "Model comparison" report lets you compare 2 different attribution models side-by-side. To find keywords, ad groups, campaigns, or devices that are undervalued on a last-click basis, you can compare the "Last click" model to the "Data-driven" model to view the value of keywords as determined by Google AI, which looks at how your customers convert to allocate credit. Data-driven attribution also gives you a sense of the value of ad interactions along the entire conversion path.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > About the "Model comparison" report > Tip: Analyze your CPA or ROAS for different attribution models
chunks.text: You can use the "Cost / conv." and "Conv. value / cost" columns in the "Model comparison" report to compare your CPA and ROAS for different attribution models. This allows you to identify campaigns or keywords that are undervalued using the "Last click" attribution model. You can then change your bids based on the actual value of your campaigns and keywords across the full conversion path.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > How to find and set an attribution model for your conversions
chunks.text: You can set the attribution model when you're setting up your conversion action, or follow the instructions below to compare attribution models and change the attribution model for an existing conversion action:

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > How to find and set an attribution model for your conversions > Compare attribution models
chunks.text:
- Go to Attribution within the Goals menu .

- In the page menu on the left, select Model comparison.

- Select an option from the "Dimension" drop-down menu.

- Use the "Compare" and "With" drop-down menus to select the attribution models you want to view and compare.

You can search for specific keywords, ad groups, campaigns, or accounts from the search box above the table.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > How to find and set an attribution model for your conversions > Change the attribution model for an existing conversion action
chunks.text:
- Go to Summary within the Goals menu .

- In the table, choose the conversion you want to edit by selecting the conversion name.

- Select Edit settings.

- Select Attribution model, and select an attribution model from the drop-down menu.

- Select Save, and then select Done.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > How to find and set an attribution model for your conversions > Change the attribution model for an existing conversion action > Cross-account conversion tracking
chunks.text: If you use cross-account conversion tracking to track conversions at the manager account level, you must select your attribution model in the manager account.

chunks.title: About attribution models
chunks.heading: About attribution models > How to find and set an attribution model for your conversions > Attribution models in your reporting columns
chunks.text:
When you change the "Attribution model" setting for a conversion action, it only changes the way your conversions are counted in your "Conversions" and "All conversions" columns going forward. If you want to check how your historic conversions data would look with the attribution model you've just selected, you can add the "current model" columns (located in the "Attribution" section of the "Columns" menu):

- Conversions (current model)

- Cost / conv. (current model)

- Conv. rate (current model)

- Conv. value (current model)

- Conv. value / cost (current model)

- Conv. value / click (current model)

You can compare these columns to your regular conversion tracking columns to check how your data would have differed if you'd been using the attribution model you've now selected.

Like the regular "Conversions" columns, these columns won't include any conversion actions that you've chosen not to mark as primary conversions. However, cross-device conversions are included by default.
